Russ, saw UptimeHealth landed at #110 on the Inc. 5000 and is opening up Florida, North Carolina, and Georgia in 2026.

Geographic expansion usually means more healthcare accounts in play than the team can cover before reps ramp in new markets, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for UptimeHealth off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress ~4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?

Russ, quick follow-up for UptimeHealth.

Entering new metros usually means the target grows faster than the team can cover. Most teams cannot say exactly how many meetings they need to hit the new number, so the gap shows up late and the quarter turns into a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings UptimeHealth needs to close that gap this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks with every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how UptimeHealth's reply rate likely compares to other health-tech startups. Want to hop on a quick call and I will walk you through it?
